entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-3rp5-jjmw-4wv2: GitPython: git-config section-name injection enables arbitrary config directives (core.sshCommand RCE)
entry.content:
GitPython: git-config section-name injection enables arbitrary config directives (core.sshCommand RCE)

Aliases: CVE-2026-69097, PYSEC-2026-3981

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • gitpython — fixed in 3.1.53

### Summary In GitPython `<= 3.1.52`, the config writer neutralizes only CR, LF, and NUL in configuration **names**, but writes section names into the `[...]` header with no other escaping. A section/subsection name that contains `] [ "` closes the intended header and opens a second same-line section, injecting an arbitrary config directive — with no newline required. Because a submodule **name** is attacker-controlled data (it comes from a repository's `.gitmodules`, or from an application that lets a user name a submodule) and is written verbatim into the parent repository's trusted `.git/config`, an attacker can set `core.sshCommand` (or `alias.*`, `core.pager`, `core.fsmonitor`) and achieve remote code execution on the victim's next git operation. Likely **CWE-74 (Injection)**. This …

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-5xmw-vc9v-4wf2: Pillow has a heap buffer overflow with nested list coordinates
entry.content:
Pillow has a heap buffer overflow with nested list coordinates

Aliases: BIT-pillow-2026-42309, CVE-2026-42309, PYSEC-2026-2251

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H · CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • pillow — fixed in 12.2.0

Passing nested lists as coordinates to APIs that accept coordinates such as `ImagePath.Path`, `ImageDraw.ImageDraw.polygon` and `ImageDraw.ImageDraw.line` could cause a heap buffer overflow, as nested lists were recursively unpacked beyond the allocated buffer. Coordinate lists are now validated to contain exactly two numeric coordinates. This was introduced in Pillow 11.2.1.

Mercury: Stored / DOM Cross-Site Scripting (XSS): mr.Markdown renders untrusted content as raw, unsanitized HTML

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-pcc4-rvhr-2pr8: Graphify Fortran extractor: incomplete cpp #include hardening allows arbitrary host-file read/exfiltration when indexing an untrusted repo
entry.content:
Graphify Fortran extractor: incomplete cpp #include hardening allows arbitrary host-file read/exfiltration when indexing an untrusted repo

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • graphifyy — fixed in 0.9.70

## Summary The Fortran extractor's C-preprocessor step (`graphify/extractors/fortran.py`, `_cpp_preprocess`) applies an incomplete `#include` hardening. The `-nostdinc -I /dev/null` flags it relies on (comment "Security (F-007)") do **not** stop a capital-`F` Fortran source file from including **absolute paths** (`#include "/etc/passwd"`) or from **path-traversing out of the corpus** (`#include "../../../../home/victim/.ssh/id_rsa"`). `cpp` always searches the directory of the file being preprocessed for quoted includes and always honours absolute include paths, regardless of `-nostdinc`/`-I`. As a result, indexing an untrusted repository that contains a `.F`/`.F90`/`.F95`/`.F03`/`.F08` file reads arbitrary local files off the host and inlines their contents into the knowledge graph, whic…

## Summary The approval system in PraisonAI Agents caches tool approval decisions by tool name only, not by invocation arguments. Once a user approves `execute_command` for any command (e.g., `ls -la`), all subsequent `execute_command` calls in that execution context bypass the approval prompt entirely. entry.title: [UPDATED] MAL-2026-17919: Malicious code in ukraine69 (PyPI)
entry.content:
Malicious code in ukraine69 (PyPI)

Affected:

  • ukraine69

Importing `ukraine69` in versions 1.2.0–1.2.2 and 1.2.5–1.2.8 searches for local `.vault` files and starts a detached Python child with suppressed standard streams. Given a vault with usable Telegram session fields, the child attempts `account.deleteAccount` using GoyGram, with a Telethon fallback in versions 1.2.5–1.2.8. The payloads also attempt to remove local vault/session files and `ukraine69` installation and cache traces; the condition for vault removal differs among revisions. A security flaw has been discovered in vllm-project vLLM up to 0.31.0. This impacts the function get_token_bin_counts_and_mask of the file vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py of the component Penalty Handler. Performing a manipulation results in denial of service. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.
